summary.description: One-line human-readable description. Embedded for retrieval rather than the raw content — summarising before embedding cuts retrieval failures substantially (md/09 §4.4).
summary.title: Summary

ActivityCategory.description: The four capture pillars every source normalizes into.
ActivityCategory.title: ActivityCategory

ActivityPayload.description: The CAIRN-defined ``data`` section of the CloudEvent.
ActivityPayload.title: ActivityPayload

co_actors.description: Additional contributors, first-class rather than an afterthought. Squash merges collapse a branch into one commit, so pair and mob work is systematically erased unless co-authorship is modelled explicitly (md/01 §5.1).
co_actors.title: Co Actors

is_bot.description: Bot activity is retained as project context but excluded from human attribution. Dependabot can out-commit every human on a team, so filtering at the schema level means the rule cannot be forgotten by one consumer downstream.
is_bot.title: Is Bot

raw_identity.description: Identity as the source reported it — an email, handle or user ID.
raw_identity.title: Raw Identity

resolved_person_id.description: CAIRN person this resolves to. Null before identity resolution runs. One human may appear under several raw identities — a work email, a personal email, a GitHub handle — and treating those as different people would fragment their contribution record.
resolved_person_id.title: Resolved Person Id

Certainty.description:
How much CAIRN trusts a claim.

Categorical, never numeric. A "73% confident" badge looks rigorous, means
nothing to a non-technical reader, and invites false precision. Internal
numeric confidence exists for thresholds and evaluation, but it never
reaches this field or the interface (md/05 §A.2.1).
Certainty.title: Certainty

Content.description:
Optional payload detail.

Frequently absent by design. Raw diffs stay out of the pipeline by default
(md/01 §6.3) and non-work-relevant chat is excluded entirely (md/02 §7.1),
so **missing content is the normal case, not a degraded one.**
Content.title: Content

Provenance.description: Where the claim came from, and how much to trust it.

source_timestamp_ref.description: Transcript offset for meeting-derived events, enabling one-click verification (md/03 §6). Null for other sources.
source_timestamp_ref.title: Source Timestamp Ref

source_url.description: Something a human can open. Provenance is a product feature, not a debug aid.
source_url.title: Source Url

Provenance.title: Provenance

description: A CloudEvents 1.0 envelope carrying a CAIRN activity payload. Generated from apps/api/src/cairn_api/events/schema.py — edit that, not this.

actorid.description: Resolved person, mirrored onto the envelope for cheap filtering.
actorid.title: Actorid

id.description: Unique per event. Combined with `source`, this is the idempotency key — webhook redelivery is normal, so duplicates must upsert rather than create a second record (md/01 §4.1).
id.title: Id

ingestedat.description: When CAIRN received the event. Diverges from `time` routinely — backfill imports 90 days in minutes. Operational views order by this; user-facing views never do.
ingestedat.title: Ingestedat

subject.description: Entity acted upon — repository, channel or meeting identifier.
subject.title: Subject

tenantid.description: Owning workspace. Mandatory on every event, no exceptions. This lives on the envelope rather than inside the payload so that a background job cannot lose tenant context — the context is structurally inseparable from the event (md/06 §4.3).
tenantid.title: Tenantid

time.description: When the activity **happened**, not when CAIRN received it. Every user-facing view orders by this. Conflating it with ingestion time produces a brief claiming today's work that actually happened in March (md/12 §3.2).
time.title: Time

traceparent.description: W3C trace context, correlating this event with its cause (md/10 §7).
traceparent.title: Traceparent

type.description: Reverse-DNS with a version suffix, per the CloudEvents convention: ai.cairn.github.pull_request.merged.v1. The version lives in the type so a breaking change produces a new type rather than silently altering the meaning of an existing one (md/12 §4).
type.title: Type
